args.key_excerpts: "The Bachelor of Science in Artificial Intelligence has just the right blend of theory and project-based work, enabling students not only to enter industry with mastery of today's cutting-edge tools, but also to envision and develop the algorithms of tomorrow." - Anil Venkatesh, Associate Professor, "The age of artificial intelligence (AI) is here, as companies, organizations and governments worldwide are racing to create the technology to improve quality of life, enhance revenue and generate breakthrough solutions."
args.summary: Adelphi University offers a Bachelor of Science in Artificial Intelligence (AI) through its College of Arts & Sciences, located in Garden City, New York. The program is STEM-designated, allowing eligible international students to extend their OPT to 36 months. Students learn to design, build, and improve AI algorithms from a multidisciplinary perspective combining mathematics, statistics, and computer science. The program features small classes of fewer than 25 students, hands-on learning with case studies, and a 3-credit internship option. It can be completed in four years (eight semesters). Potential career paths include AI Engineer, Software Engineer, AI Systems Architect, and Data Scientist. The program also offers minors in Artificial Intelligence and Applied AI in Business, as well as the Scholar Teacher Education Program (STEP) for accelerated master's degrees. Related programs include Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, and graduate degrees in AI/ML. The program is open to well-qualified first-year, transfer, and international students. Students can also apply for The Honors College, Levermore Global Scholars, and Study Abroad opportunities. The program is led by the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science, chaired by Dr. Kees Leune.

A "Tiangong" humanoid robot displays running at the Beijng World of Robots in Beijing, capital of China, Feb. 24, 2025. (Xinhua/Ju Huanzong)

China's prestigious Tsinghua University announced Sunday that it will establish a new undergraduate school focused on developing talent in artificial intelligence (AI).

The university plans to enroll about 150 students in the new school this year.

The new school will emphasize AI's role in education and research, integrating AI with multiple disciplines. It aims to develop a new model for AI-driven education while training students with strong AI literacy, technical expertise and innovative capabilities.

According to the university's academic affairs office, Tsinghua has already made strides in AI education. It has introduced 117 pilot courses and 147 classes incorporating AI-driven teaching methods. It has also developed tools such as intelligent teaching assistants, lesson-planning aids and automated grading systems.

# Artificial Intelligence Education in China: Report on University Programs and Eligibility Criteria

**I. [Introduction](https://omicstutorials.com/what-is-the-difference-between-bioinformatics-and-computational-biology/)**

The field of [artificial intelligence](https://omicstutorials.com/from-sample-to-sequence-a-comprehensive-guide-to-protein-sequencing-and-bioinformatics-analysis/) ([AI](https://omicstutorials.com/how-are-big-data-ai-and-health-informatics-improving-healthcare-outcomes/)) has emerged as a transformative force across numerous sectors globally, driving innovation and shaping the future of technology. Recognizing the strategic importance of AI, China has made significant investments in fostering a robust ecosystem for AI [research and development](https://omicstutorials.com/how-has-high-throughput-sequencing-impacted-the-field-of-bioinformatics/), including a strong emphasis on education and talent cultivation. This report provides a comprehensive [analysis](https://omicstutorials.com/what-is-the-difference-between-bioinformatics-and-computational-biology/) of the landscape of AI-related academic programs offered by leading universities and colleges in China, targeting prospective international [students](https://omicstutorials.com/top-10-ai-studying-tools-to-boost-your-productivity/) seeking undergraduate, Master’s, or PhD degrees in this dynamic field. The information presented herein is based on a thorough examination of recent data and announcements from various academic institutions and relevant online resources. The aim is to offer a detailed guide to the available programs, their geographical distribution across China, and the specific eligibility criteria that international applicants must meet to gain admission.

**II. Methodology**

The information contained in this report has been compiled through a meticulous process of analyzing publicly available data and resources. This involved a detailed review of [university](https://omicstutorials.com/the-ultimate-guide-to-bioinformatics-internships/) websites, admissions portals, and educational platforms that provide information on academic programs offered to international students in China. The focus of this analysis was to identify universities providing [degree programs](https://omicstutorials.com/exploring-future-professions-10-exceptional-career-paths/) specifically in Artificial Intelligence or closely related fields such as [Computer Science](https://omicstutorials.com/what-is-the-difference-between-bioinformatics-and-computational-biology/) with an AI specialization. For each identified institution, information pertaining to undergraduate, Master’s, and PhD programs was sought. Special attention was paid to the specific eligibility criteria for each program level, including academic prerequisites, language proficiency requirements (both English and Chinese), and any additional qualifications such as [research](https://omicstutorials.com/what-visualization-tools-show-multi-omics-data-together/) experience or specific subject knowledge. The collected data was then organized geographically, categorized by province or major administrative division, to provide a structured and easily navigable overview of AI education opportunities across China.

**III. Landscape of AI Education in China: Top Universities and [Emerging Trends](https://omicstutorials.com/multi-omics-in-biological-research-integrating-data-for-advanced-insights/)**

China is rapidly establishing itself as a global hub for AI research and education, with several of its universities achieving top international rankings in this domain . Among these leading institutions, Tsinghua University stands out as a prominent center for AI studies, holding the top position in Asia for AI and ranking among the top three globally for Computer Science . Tsinghua University has demonstrated a strong commitment to advancing AI through the establishment of a dedicated College of AI, an initiative focused on fostering [interdisciplinary](https://omicstutorials.com/data-science-for-bioinformatics/) innovation and cultivating top-tier talent in the field . This strategic move underscores the university’s ambition to be at the forefront of [AI development](https://omicstutorials.com/unlocking-ai-excellence-dive-into-top-projects-platforms-with-our-ultimate-guide/) and education.  

Similarly, Shanghai Jiao Tong University is recognized for its strong emphasis on AI and [data science](https://omicstutorials.com/frequently-searched-questions-in-bioinformatics/), actively concentrating on frontier [technologies](https://omicstutorials.com/what-computational-problems-are-encountered-in-sequence-assembly/) and emerging [industries](https://omicstutorials.com/what-careers-or-industries-use-bioinformatics/) crucial for national development . The university’s AI research center collaborates extensively with various technology companies to develop innovative solutions in AI [applications](https://omicstutorials.com/what-is-the-difference-between-bioinformatics-and-computational-biology/), ensuring its curriculum remains relevant to the evolving demands of the AI landscape . Fudan University has also launched significant initiatives to cultivate interdisciplinary AI talent through innovative programs and research, with plans to introduce at least 100 AI-related courses in the 2024-25 academic year . This initiative aims to transform the university into a leading force in science intelligence education and talent cultivation, further highlighting the growing importance of AI across academic disciplines.   

Zhejiang University is another institution recognized for its interdisciplinary approach to AI research, integrating fields such as robotics, [big data](https://omicstutorials.com/quick-guide-tutorial-challenges-in-big-data-and-bioinformatics/), and cognitive computing . The university’s AI [research initiatives](https://omicstutorials.com/what-are-some-of-the-challenges-and-limitations-of-bioinformatics/) are focused on real-world applications, positioning it as a leader in practical AI solutions. The University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) is also known for its cutting-edge research in AI, having produced numerous influential papers in the field, with a research focus on areas such as [machine learning](https://omicstutorials.com/essential-tools-and-software-in-bioinformatics-blast-fasta-and-clustal-2/) [algorithms](https://omicstutorials.com/what-exactly-is-bioinformatics-an-in-depth-analysis/) and [AI ethics](https://omicstutorials.com/googles-gemini-a-multimodal-masterpiece-unveiled/) . These examples illustrate the commitment of China’s top universities to expanding and enhancing their AI-related academic offerings.  

A notable observation is the close [relationship](https://omicstutorials.com/what-is-the-difference-between-bioinformatics-and-computational-biology/) between top AI programs and established Computer Science departments . Universities with a strong foundation in Computer Science often serve as the base for the development of comprehensive AI programs. This connection is logical as AI inherently relies on core [computer science principles](https://omicstutorials.com/how-does-bioinformatics-connect-computer-science-it-and-biology/), algorithms, and data structures. The consistent appearance of the same universities in rankings for both AI and Computer Science reflects this underlying interconnectedness.   

Furthermore, there is a clear trend among leading Chinese universities to actively expand their AI-related academic programs and increase student enrollment in these areas . This expansion is frequently accompanied by the creation of new AI-focused schools or departments and the introduction of innovative, interdisciplinary AI curricula. This trend likely reflects the Chinese government’s strategic focus on AI as a critical technology for national progress and global competitiveness. Universities are responding to this national priority by strengthening their AI education capabilities to meet the anticipated high demand for AI professionals. This expansion signifies increasing opportunities for both domestic and international students interested in specializing in AI within China.   

**IV. State-wise List of Universities Offering AI Programs and Eligibility Criteria**

This section provides a state-wise breakdown of universities in China offering Artificial Intelligence programs at the undergraduate, Master’s, and PhD levels, along with their respective eligibility criteria for international students.

**A. Beijing**

* **1. Tsinghua University:**

  + **Undergraduate AI Program(s):** Tsinghua University, consistently ranked as a premier institution for AI, offers various undergraduate programs, including those taught in English .
    - Eligibility Criteria:
      * General Admission: Foreign citizens in good health, friendly towards China, holding a high school graduation certificate .
      * Academic Performance: Demonstrated outstanding academic performance through transcripts, graduation/matriculation exam results, and standardized test scores (e.g., SAT, ACT, A-Level, IB) .
      * Language Proficiency:
        + English-taught programs: High level of English proficiency required, with test reports (TOEFL, IELTS) for non-native speakers .
        + Chinese-English taught programs: HSK Level 5 (score > 60 in each subject) or initial HSK Level 4 (must reach Level 5 within the first year). Native Chinese speakers or those with Chinese high school education may apply for an HSK waiver. High English proficiency also required .
      * Age: Minimum 18 years old by September 1, 2025. Applicants under 18 need to provide additional documents .
      * Other: Compliance with Document No. 12 (2020) of the Ministry of Education of the PRC .
  + **Master’s AI Program(s):** Tsinghua University offers Master’s level AI programs, building on its strong foundation in computer science and technology .
    - Eligibility Criteria:
      * Citizenship: Non-Chinese citizens with a valid personal ordinary passport .
      * Educational Background: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent from a recognized institution, obtained before the 2025 registration date. Degrees from overseas universities require CSCSE authentication; mainland degrees require CSSD authentication .
      * Health and Conduct: Good physical and [mental health](https://omicstutorials.com/ai-driven-revolution-in-clinical-document-parsing-improving-heart-failure-diagnosis/), good moral character, abiding by Chinese laws and university rules .
      * Language Proficiency: Specific requirements vary by program, as detailed in the Catalog of Graduate Programs 2025. Generally, HSK Level 5 or above may be required, and English proficiency is expected .
      * Academic Transcript: Undergraduate transcript required. GPA certification needed if not on the transcript. Final transcript required before registration for current students .
      * Degree Certificate and Authentication: Bachelor’s degree certificate required. Overseas degrees need CSCSE authentication; mainland degrees need CSSD authentication. Expected graduation certificate is acceptable initially, with the degree and authentication needed before registration .
      * Additional Documents: Personal statement, passport copy, two academic recommendation letters .
  + **PhD AI Program(s):** Tsinghua University provides doctoral programs in AI, attracting top research aspirants .
    - Eligibility Criteria:
      * Citizenship: Non-Chinese citizens with a valid personal ordinary passport .
      * Educational Background: Master’s degree or equivalent. Exceptional Bachelor’s degree holders may apply directly under specific conditions .
      * Health and Character: Good health and moral character, willingness to abide by laws and regulations .
      * GPA (for Bachelor’s to PhD): Minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.5/4.0 or B+ or 85/100 .
      * Language Proficiency:
        + Bachelor’s to PhD: HSK band 4 (score > 195), with potential exemptions for English-taught programs .
        + Non-native English speakers: TOEFL > 85 or IELTS > 6.5 .
        + General AI PhD: Requires English fluency .
      * Academic Transcripts: Transcripts from undergraduate and [graduate studies](https://omicstutorials.com/career-guidance-outline-for-bioinformatics/) (if applicable) .
      * Degree Certificates and Authentication: Bachelor’s and Master’s certificates (if applicable) with CSCSE/CSSD authentication .
      * Personal Statement and Research Plan: Detailed statement and comprehensive research plan required .
      * Letters of Recommendation: Two academic recommendations from associate professors or higher. For Bachelor’s to PhD applicants, letters should attest to research ability .
      * Passport: Valid personal ordinary-type passport .
* **2. Peking University:**

  + **Undergraduate AI Program(s):** Peking University is a highly regarded institution offering undergraduate programs, including those in AI-related fields .
    - Eligibility Criteria:
      * Nationality: Non-Chinese citizens with a valid passport. Specific rules for former Chinese citizens .
      * Health and Conduct: Good physical and mental health, no criminal record, compliance with laws and regulations .
      * Educational Background: Full-time high school graduation degree (excluding Chinese ordinary high schools). Primary to high school education should align with an overseas system .
      * Age: Typically 17-23 years old .
      * Language Proficiency:
        + Chinese-taught: HSK Level 6 (score > 200, [writing](https://omicstutorials.com/top-10-ai-studying-tools-to-boost-your-productivity/) > 65). Some sources mention HSK Level 5 .
        + English-taught: TOEFL iBT > 75 (undergrad), > 100 (grad) or IELTS > 6.5 (undergrad), > 7.0 (grad) .
      * Academic Transcript: Original high school transcript. Notarized [translation](https://omicstutorials.com/introduction-to-bioinformatics-for-computer-science-students/) if not in English or Chinese .
      * Personal Statement: In Chinese or English .
      * Letters of Recommendation: Two original letters, one from a high school teacher/head teacher .
      * Passport Copy: Valid passport with expiry beyond July 2025 .
      * Letter of Commitment: Signed letter in Chinese or English .
      * Optional Materials: SAT, IB, A-Levels, ACT scores, other awards, HSK transcripts .
      * Entrance Examination: May be required (Chinese, English, Mathematics). Exemption possible with high standardized test scores .
  + **Master’s AI Program(s):** Peking University offers Master’s programs in AI-related fields, building on its strong academic reputation .
    - Eligibility Criteria:
      * Nationality: Non-Chinese citizens with a valid passport. Specific rules for former Chinese citizens .
      * Health and Conduct: Good physical and mental health, no criminal record, compliance with laws and regulations .
      * Educational Background: Bachelor’s degree from a university accredited by the Ministry of Education of China. No grade skipping or mid-course joining .
      * Language Proficiency:
        + Chinese-taught (Science & Engineering): HSK Level 6 (score > 200, writing > 65) .
        + English-taught: TOEFL iBT > 100 or GRE > 320 or IELTS > 6.5. Some sources mention slightly different scores . Exemption for degrees from English-speaking countries/institutions.
      * Academic Transcript: Official undergraduate transcript, translated and notarized if needed .
      * Personal Statement: Including a research plan (around 1500 words) .
      * Letters of Recommendation: Two letters from professors/associate professors in the applicant’s major .
      * Passport Copy: Valid passport with expiry after December 2025 .
      * Degree Certificate and Authentication: Original Bachelor’s degree certificate and authentication (CSCSE for overseas, CSSD for mainland) .
      * Resume and Commitment: Resume and signed Commitment for Application .
      * Publications: Table of contents and abstracts if applicable .
  + **PhD AI Program(s):** Peking University offers doctoral programs in AI and related fields, attracting advanced researchers .
    - Eligibility Criteria:
      * Nationality: Non-Chinese citizens with a valid passport. Specific rules for former Chinese citizens .
      * Health and Conduct: Good physical and mental health, no criminal record, compliance with laws and regulations .
      * Educational Background: Master’s degree from a recognized institution. Bachelor’s degree holders in science and engineering may apply directly .
      * Language Proficiency:
        + Chinese-taught (Science): HSK Level 6 (score > 200, writing > 65) .
        + English-taught: TOEFL iBT > 100 or GRE > 320 or IELTS > 6.5. Exemption for degrees from English-speaking countries/institutions .
      * Academic Transcripts: Transcripts from undergraduate and graduate studies .
      * Personal Statement and Research Plan: Detailed statement including a comprehensive research plan (around 3000 words). Indicate desired supervisor .
      * Letters of Recommendation: Two letters from professors/associate professors in the applicant’s major .
      * Passport Copy: Valid ordinary passport with expiry after December 2025 .
      * Degree Certificates and Authentication: Bachelor’s and Master’s certificates with CSCSE/CSSD authentication .
      * Resume and Commitment: Resume and signed “Commitment for Application” .
      * Publications: Table of contents and abstracts if applicable .

**B. Shanghai**

* **1. Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU):**
  + **Undergraduate AI Program(s):** SJTU is a leading university with AI programs at the undergraduate level .
    - Eligibility Criteria:

      * Citizenship: Non-Chinese citizens with a foreign passport, complying with Document No. 12 (2020) of MOE .
      * Language Proficiency:
        + Chinese: HSK Level 5 (score > 200, writing > 60) or HSK Level 6 (score > 180, writing > 60), or proof of native Chinese speaker .
        + English: TOEFL (code: D070) or IELTS report, or other proof (e.g., native speaker, English study certificates) . TOEFL iBT > 84 or IELTS > 6.0 also mentioned .
      * Entrance Exam: Required for applicants passing the preliminary review, includes online written and oral tests (Math, Physics, English, Chinese I & II) .
      * Additional Documents: High school diploma, transcripts, language certificates, passport, parent’s passport, personal statement, two recommendation letters .
  + **Master’s AI Program(s):** SJTU offers Master’s programs in AI and related fields .
    - Eligibility Criteria:
      * Citizenship: Non-Chinese citizen .
      * Health: Good physical and mental health .
      * Academic Performance: Outstanding academic performance and potential .
      * Educational Background: Bachelor’s degree required .
      * Language Proficiency: Proficiency in Chinese and/or English. Details at <https://isc.sjtu.edu.cn/EN/content.aspx?info_lb=185&flag=2> . TOEFL iBT > 79 or IELTS > 6.0 or TOEIC > 800 mentioned for some programs .
      * Application Materials: Online application, degree certificates, transcripts, language proficiency proof, passport, photo, personal statement, study plan, two recommendation letters .
  + **PhD AI Program(s):** SJTU provides doctoral programs in Computer Science and Technology with AI specializations .
    - Eligibility Criteria:
      * Educational Background: Master’s degree required .
      * Transcripts: Undergraduate and graduate transcripts required .
      * Language Proficiency: English-taught program. Proof of English proficiency required. TOEFL iBT > 85. GRE (Verbal > 160, Quantitative > 160, Analytical > 3.5) and GMAT (> 550) also mentioned .
      * Additional Materials: Degree certificates, passport copy, photo, personal statement, study plan, two academic recommendation letters . Contacting supervisor beforehand may be needed for some schools .

**V. Conclusion**

This report has illuminated the extensive opportunities available for international students seeking to pursue academic degrees in Artificial Intelligence within China. Leading universities across the country, particularly in major educational hubs like Beijing, Shanghai, and Zhejiang, offer comprehensive programs at the undergraduate, Master’s, and PhD levels. These institutions are not only recognized for their academic excellence and global rankings but are also actively expanding their AI-related offerings, reflecting China’s national strategic focus on this transformative technology.

Prospective international students must recognize the importance of consulting the official websites of their target universities and specific programs. The eligibility criteria outlined in this report provide a general overview, but the most accurate, detailed, and up-to-date information regarding admission requirements, application procedures, deadlines, and program-specific prerequisites will always be found on the official university sources.

A critical factor for international applicants is the language of instruction for their chosen program. Many programs are offered in English, while others are taught in Chinese or a combination of both. Therefore, students must carefully assess their language proficiency in either English or Chinese and ensure they meet the stipulated requirements, including achieving the necessary scores on standardized tests such as TOEFL, IELTS, and HSK.

While this report has primarily focused on academic eligibility criteria, international students should also plan for other essential aspects of studying abroad, such as the student visa application process, exploring accommodation options (both on-campus and off-campus), and understanding the estimated costs associated with tuition fees and living expenses in China.

In conclusion, China offers a vibrant and rapidly growing environment for international students to receive high-quality education in Artificial Intelligence. The country’s increasing prominence in AI research and application, coupled with the commitment of its leading universities to academic excellence in this field, presents compelling opportunities for students worldwide to advance their knowledge and [careers](https://omicstutorials.com/what-careers-or-industries-use-bioinformatics/) in AI.

args.summary:
This webpage is a comprehensive report on Artificial Intelligence (AI) education in China, targeting prospective international students seeking undergraduate, Master's, or PhD degrees. Published on March 28, 2025, on Omics tutorials, the report analyzes AI programs at leading Chinese universities, their geographical distribution, and eligibility criteria.

Key findings include:
- China is rapidly becoming a global AI education hub, with Tsinghua University ranking top in Asia for AI.
- Top universities (Tsinghua, Peking, Zhejiang, Shanghai Jiao Tong, USTC) are actively expanding AI programs, creating new AI-focused schools, and increasing enrollment, reflecting China's national strategic focus on AI.
- There is a strong connection between top AI programs and established Computer Science departments.

Detailed eligibility criteria are provided for international students at major universities across Beijing, Shanghai, Zhejiang, and Anhui provinces, covering:
- **Tsinghua University (Beijing):** Undergraduate requires high school diploma, HSK Level 5+ (Chinese programs) or TOEFL/IELTS (English programs), minimum age 18. Master's requires Bachelor's degree, HSK Level 5+ likely, two recommendation letters. PhD requires Master's degree (or exceptional Bachelor's with 3.5/4.0 GPA), TOEFL > 85 or IELTS > 6.5, research plan.
- **Peking University (Beijing):** Undergraduate requires HSK Level 6 (>200, writing >65) for Chinese-taught or TOEFL iBT >75 for English-taught, age 17-23. Master's requires Bachelor's degree, HSK Level 6 or TOEFL iBT >100/GRE >320/IELTS >6.5, two recommendation letters. PhD requires Master's degree, similar language requirements, detailed research plan (~3000 words).
- **Shanghai Jiao Tong University (Shanghai):** Undergraduate requires high school diploma, HSK Level 5+ or TOEFL iBT >84/IELTS >6.0, entrance exam. Master's requires Bachelor's degree, TOEFL iBT >79 or IELTS >6.0 or TOEIC >800. PhD requires Master's degree, TOEFL iBT >85, GRE may be required.
- **Zhejiang University (Zhejiang):** Undergraduate requires high school diploma, HSK Level 4+ (Chinese) or IELTS 5.5/TOEFL 60+ (English), age under 25. Master's requires Bachelor's degree, HSK Level 5+ or IELTS 6.0/TOEFL 80+. PhD requires Master's degree, similar language requirements, research proposal required.
- **University of Science and Technology of China (Anhui):** Undergraduate requires high school diploma, HSK Level 4 (Chinese) or TOEFL >80/IELTS >6.0 (English). Master's requires Bachelor's degree, HSK Level 4+ or IELTS >6.5/TOEFL >80. PhD requires Master's degree, HSK Level 4+ or IELTS >6/TOEFL >80.

The report includes two key tables: one listing top AI universities by province with their strengths, and another summarizing language proficiency requirements across all degree levels. It emphasizes that prospective students should always consult official university websites for the most current information and plan for visa, accommodation, and costs.

Several of China's top universities have declared plans to expand undergraduate enrollment in 2025, with a sharp focus on national strategic priorities and cutting-edge technologies.

Both Tsinghua and Peking universities announced plans to expand their undergraduate intake by around 150 undergraduate spots each. Tsinghua University will establish a new undergraduate general education college to focus on cultivating interdisciplinary talents in artificial intelligence (AI). The new enrollment plan of Peking University will center on fields of national strategic needs, fundamental disciplines, and emerging frontiers.

Renmin University will add over 100 places in areas such as AI. Other institutions, such as Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Wuhan University, are expanding places in AI, renewable energy, and integrated circuits to meet national strategic needs.

The 2025 government work report emphasizes the importance of continuously promoting the "AI Plus" initiative, aiming to better integrate digital technology with manufacturing and market strengths. It advocates for extensive application of large language models and the development of next-generation intelligent products.

China in January issued its first national action plan to build a "strong education nation" by 2035, to help coordinate its education development, improve efficiency in innovation and build a "strong country."

# Inside China's top computer science university training the next generation of AI engineers

By   [Lee Chong Ming](https://www.businessinsider.com/author/lee-chong-ming) 

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

![Tsinghua university](https://i.insider.com/69eae852367066d7c2970711?width=700)

  

Tsinghua students tell BI they study long hours, join research labs, and publish multiple papers to build a future in AI.  CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images

[Read in app](https://insider-app.onelink.me/4cpG/?af_js_web=true&af_ss_ver=2_3_0&af_dp=insider%3A%2F%2Fbi%2Fpost%2Finside-tsinghua-china-computer-science-school-training-ai-engineers-talent-2026-4&af_force_deeplink=true&is_retargeting=true&deep_link_value=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.businessinsider.com%2Finside-tsinghua-china-computer-science-school-training-ai-engineers-talent-2026-4&pid=businessinsider&c=post_page_share_bar_v2_smart_4.13.23 "Download the app")

This story is available exclusively to Business Insider subscribers. [Become an Insider](/subscription) and start reading now. Have an account? .

Felix Gan, a second-year Ph.D. student in computer science, said he is effectively living a ["996" routine](https://www.businessinsider.com/996-china-games-designer-jack-forsdike-working-hours-culture-office-2024-9) atBeijing's Tsinghua University. Seven days a week, his days start around 8 a.m., and he leaves campusat about 9 p.m.

Most of those hours go into his research, but he's not just working toward a degree. Gan hopes to develop a technology he can turn into a product and launch a startup after graduation.

That level of intensity is the norm on campus, where writing one thesis isn't enough to stand out. Some students write several.

Tsinghua is China's top computer science university, often likened to Harvard University or Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Students are gearing up for a front-row seat in the [global AI race](https://www.businessinsider.com/china-deepseek-integrate-ai-consolidation-us-openai-paywall-2025-4).

As China's AI ambitions grow, so does the pressure on the engineers and researchers in training.

Many say the payoff for years of hardcore schooling is worth it. Making it through Tsinghua can mean [a golden ticket](https://www.businessinsider.com/american-studied-china-universities-cheaper-2026-3) into the ranks of China's tech elite — a network that includes the likes of Wang Xing, the cofounder and CEO of Meituan, one of China's largest on-demand services companies. Other notable Tsinghua alumni include China's president, Xi Jinping, and his predecessor, Hu Jintao.

Tsinghua alumni have founded more than 1,000 companies, including over a dozen unicorns, according to market intelligence platform Tracxn.

[### Explore BI Games

Take a smarter break in your day - and see how far you get.

Play now

![](/public/assets/games/games-discovery/discover-sm.png)](/games)

## **Normalized 'grind' culture**

The university is among the most selective in China. To get in, students need top marks on the Gaokao, China's national college entrance exam.

In 2024, only about 0.05% of Gaokao test-takers made it into Tsinghua or Peking University combined — roughly one in 2,000 students, according to national data cited by Chinese media.

Tsinghua's undergraduate student body largely comes from mainland China. Graduate schools have more international students, like Tsinghua University Shenzhen International Graduate School. Located about 1,400 miles south of Beijing, the graduate school brings together Chinese and international students in research-driven, industry-linked programs.

Daniyar Kuzekov, a master's student studying data science and information tech at Tsinghua's Shenzhen Institute of Graduate Studies, said most students he meets either have exceptional backgrounds or are relentless grinding.

"I feel the pressure that they were on before, how hardworking they were in order to get here to this level," he added.

Kuzekov, who's from Kazakhstan, described locking into a 22-hour straight coding marathon for his thesis, working alongside an AI assistant on a paper about DeepSeek.

![Daniyar Kuzekov](data:image/svg+xml,%3C%3Fxml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'%3F%3E%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='1' height='1'/%3E)

 

Daniyar Kuzekov said he can rely on Tsinghua to build his reputation because of the school's close ties to the tech industry.   Daniyar Kuzekov

  

Students told Business Insider that the grind culture comes with learning at the AI frontier. For computer science undergraduate Pau Tong Lin Xu, late nights and seven to eight hours of studying a day are typical.

"You learn a lot, but that comes at the cost of a huge workload, and sometimes that can leave little time for you to do other things or explore some of your own ideas," he said.

He described the peer pressure as a "double-edged sword" — motivating, yet at times overwhelming.

Tsinghua's culture reflects a broader trend in China, often described as "involution" — a cycle of intense competition in which everyone works harder just to keep up.

[Some young Chinese people](https://www.businessinsider.com/china-rat-people-broke-burnt-out-social-media-unemployment-2025-4) have pushed back by "lying flat," [rejecting the grind](https://www.businessinsider.com/china-economy-college-grads-lying-flat-zombie-photos-youth-unemployment-2023-7). But for students at elite universities, opting out is rarely an option.

![Pau Tong Lin Xu](data:image/svg+xml,%3C%3Fxml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'%3F%3E%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='1' height='1'/%3E)

 

Pau Tong Lin Xu, an undergraduate computer science student, said it is common to study for 7 to 8 hours a day.   Pau Tong Lin Xu

  

## Publishing early, joining labs, coding as baseline

Beyond the daily grind, many computer science majors join research labs early and work on academic papers.

Some undergraduates go a step further, aiming to publish at top-tier computer science conferences — a signal of research ability when applying to graduate programs.

Zhixun Tan, who graduated with a bachelor's degree in electronic engineering in 2016 and works as a software engineer at Google, said joining research labs and engaging in out-of-classroom activities were the most valuable parts of his Tsinghua experience.

Professors were happy to guide students in research programs. "You can just reach out randomly to professors, and more often than not, they will happily take you," Tan said.

Tan completed a summer research program at Imperial College London organized by his school, which he said broadened his research horizons.

![Zhixun Tan](data:image/svg+xml,%3C%3Fxml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'%3F%3E%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='1' height='1'/%3E)

 

Zhixun Tan, who graduated in 2016 and now works as a software engineer at Google, said research opportunities abroad and joining labs broadened his educational horizons.   Zhixun Tan

  

Davenzka Abigayle, a second-year undergraduate student majoring in biomedical engineering, said coding is treated as a baseline skill across disciplines at Tsinghua. Economics students might pick up Python for data analysis. Science and engineering students often go deeper, learning languages like C++ early on, she said.

Abigayle completed her C++ course in her first semester.

"It's useful in the long run," she said, adding that coding has helped in her coursework and projects.

Students also use AI tools daily to [supercharge learning](https://www.businessinsider.com/china-beijing-ai-education-mandatory-classrooms-elementary-schoolers-2025-3).

For Gan, the Ph.D. student, AI tripled his research speed, helping with preliminary checks, drafting code, and early implementations. But the final step remains manual.

"Professors are telling you use the tools, don't resist the tools, but we do still need to validate our code manually at the end because research requires exact precision," he said.

Kuzekov said he uses [AI tools](https://www.businessinsider.com/deepseek-new-ai-training-models-scale-manifold-constrained-analysts-china-2026-1) in his machine learning course with his professor's approval.

"We have to share our chats and all of these materials with our teacher," he said.

In some classes, students disclose how much of their work involved AI. Professors can also cross-check usage to verify their work, Abigayle said.

Zak Dychtwald, the founder of the Young China Group, a think tank based in Shanghai, said Tsinghua's prestige "comes from being China's most selective, best-resourced, and most symbolically important university, with especially strong engineering and computer science pipelines that translate directly into elite jobs and AI research.

"As China is increasingly recognized as sourcing the world's leading AI talent, the name recognition has even more significance than it used to," he added.

![Felix Gan](data:image/svg+xml,%3C%3Fxml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'%3F%3E%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='1' height='1'/%3E)

 

Felix Gan, a Ph.D. student in computer science, said he works long hours on campus.   Felix Gan

  

## A ticket to the top

For many students, the benefits of enrolling at Tsinghua become apparent quickly.

Bryan Constantine Sadihin, a second-year master's student studying computer science, said Tsinghua's training gives him an edge in highly competitive technical interviews.

A year into his program, he secured a research internship at ShengShu, one of China's leading AI startups, where he worked on multimodal generative AI models. He said Tsinghua's reputation and training make him "optimistic" about his job prospects.

![Bryan Constantine Sadihin](data:image/svg+xml,%3C%3Fxml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'%3F%3E%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='1' height='1'/%3E)

 

Bryan Constantine Sadihin, a second-year master's student studying computer science, says Tsinghua prepares him well for technical interviews.   Bryan Constantine Sadihin

  

Tech-related roles are the biggest destination. About a third of Tsinghua undergraduates entered IT and software-related industries in 2022, according to the university's data.

Zhao Litao, a senior research fellow with the East Asian Institute at the National University of Singapore, said Tsinghua sits at the apex of China's higher education.

"Its prestige reflects not only academic strength but also its historical role in training political, scientific, and technological elites," said Zhao, who researches China's social policy.

Zhao said Tsinghua graduates typically move into "leading tech firms, high-growth startups, or pursue further study." Preferred tech employers include Huawei, ByteDance, Tencent, and Alibaba.

Academia remains a key path, with many staying in China as geopolitical tensions rise and local opportunities expand, Zhao said.

"Notably, a smaller but influential segment moves into AI-focused startups, often linked to university labs," he added.

## Front-row seat to China's AI ambition

As China closes the gap with — and in some areas challenges — the [US in AI](https://www.businessinsider.com/elon-musk-china-ai-compute-exceed-electricity-power-2026-1), Tsinghua students know they are in the heart of it.

Tan, the Google software engineer, said it was clear even as an undergraduate in the mid-2010s that China was at the [forefront of technology](https://www.businessinsider.com/china-deepseek-integrate-ai-consolidation-us-openai-paywall-2025-4) and rapidly producing tech talent.

Zhao, the NUS research fellow, said that China's university system is increasingly structured to channel top talent into strategically important sectors — AI being one of the top priorities.

Backed by strong state support and rapid industry growth, the field is widely seen as the frontier of both scientific progress and economic opportunity.

"This is not purely a top-down process — student preferences, labor market signals, and institutional incentives are reinforcing each other, especially in AI," he added.

For some Tsinghua students and alumni, being part of China's top AI training grounds comes with a sense of responsibility to lead the tech revolution.

"There's nobody to fix the problem except us. So we have to step up and do the most difficult things, and then other people will follow suit," Tan said.

# Top 10 AI Programs in China for International Students

*— Where the Future is Being Built*

Artificial intelligence is now a major study field. It shapes healthcare, finance, education, robotics, transport, and online services.

China plays a major role in this field. The country has strong **Chinese universities**, large technology firms, and active **AI research**.

This guide covers the **top 10 AI programs in China** for foreign students. It also explains what each school offers and how to choose the right program.

Students who plan to [study in China](https://applyforchina.com/) can use this guide to compare options in Beijing, Shanghai, Hangzhou, Nanjing, Hefei, Harbin, and Xi’an.

## Quick Answer: Top 10 AI Programs in China

Here are the **top 10 AI programs in China** in this guide:

|  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Rank | University | City | Strong Areas |
| 1 | Tsinghua University | Beijing | AI research, computer science, algorithms |
| 2 | Peking University | Beijing | AI theory, data science, AI ethics |
| 3 | Shanghai Jiao Tong University | Shanghai | Robotics, machine learning, smart systems |
| 4 | Zhejiang University | Hangzhou | AI, cloud computing, smart cities |
| 5 | Nanjing University | Nanjing | Machine learning, NLP, cognitive science |
| 6 | University of Science and Technology of China | Hefei | Robotics, automation, science research |
| 7 | Beihang University | Beijing | Aerospace AI, UAVs, computer vision |
| 8 | Harbin Institute of Technology | Harbin | Engineering AI, intelligent control |
| 9 | Xidian University | Xi’an | Cyber systems, signal processing, AI security |
| 10 | Fudan University | Shanghai | Data science, medical AI, AI ethics |

## **Why Study AI in China?**

Why Study Artificial Intelligence in China?

China has built a large AI education and research system. Many universities work with research labs, technology firms, and local government projects.

Students can learn **artificial intelligence in China** through:

* computer science
* machine learning
* robotics
* data science
* natural language processing
* **computer vision**
* intelligent systems
* AI ethics
* software engineering

Many **international students in China** also study with Chinese students. This gives them a closer look at China’s tech culture and classroom style.

China also treats AI as a key part of national **research and development**. Government policy, the **Ministry of Education**, local government plans, and national **year plans** support science and technology growth.

China’s AI policy also connects with global issues. These include **export controls**, chip supply, data rules, and large scale AI development. This makes China a useful place to understand both education and real-world **China technology**.

## What Do AI Programs in China Teach?

Most **AI programs in China** start with computer science and math.

Students usually study:

* programming
* algorithms
* calculus and linear algebra
* probability and statistics
* machine learning
* deep learning
* database systems
* robotics
* computer vision
* natural language processing
* AI project design

At master’s and PhD level, students focus on research. Common topics include AI safety, large language models, smart robotics, medical AI, and intelligent manufacturing.

Some programs teach in English. Many programs teach in Chinese. Students should check the language before applying.

## **The Top 10 AI Programs in China**

Here are ten Chinese universities that are leading the way in AI education, and why they deserve your attention.

### **1. [Tsinghua University](https://applyforchina.com/universities/tsinghua-university/) (Beijing)**

**Tsinghua University** is one of the strongest choices for AI in China. Often called “China’s MIT,” Tsinghua has a world-class reputation in computer science, engineering, automation, and electronic information. Its AI research connects with national projects, Beijing research institutes, and leading technology companies. The university also has a College of AI, which supports innovation, top-tier talent training, and research in deep learning, natural language processing, and computer vision.

Tsinghua is a good choice for students who want:

* a program often compared with MIT, Stanford, and other global leaders
* high quality AI research
* strong computer science training
* access to Beijing’s research network
* links with national labs and technology firms

### **2. [Peking University](https://applyforchina.com/universities/peking-university/) (Beijing)**

**Peking University** is another top choice for students who want to study AI in China. The university combines strong training in computer science, math, data science, and AI theory with broad interdisciplinary research. Its AI-related study can connect with ethics, policy, healthcare, economics, and language technology.

Peking University also benefits from its Beijing location. Students can access leading universities, research institutes, policy circles, and major technology companies. This makes the university a strong option for students who want both academic depth and career opportunities.

Peking University is a good choice for students who want:

* access to Beijing’s research and technology network
* theory-based AI study
* strong computer science and data science training
* AI ethics and policy research
* interdisciplinary AI applications

### **3. [Shanghai Jiao Tong University](https://applyforchina.com/universities/sjtu/) (Shanghai)**

**Shanghai Jiao Tong University** is a strong choice for students who want engineering-based AI training in a major business city. SJTU has a strong reputation in applied AI, especially in robotics, machine learning, intelligent systems, automation, and smart manufacturing.

Its School of Electronic Information and Electrical Engineering supports AI-related study through computer science, electronic information, and intelligent technology fields. Students can also benefit from Shanghai’s global business environment, where AI connects with finance, trade, technology, and advanced manufacturing.

SJTU is a good choice for students who want:

* AI study linked with business and technology
* practical AI education
* robotics and machine learning
* intelligent systems and automation
* industry exposure in Shanghai

### **4. [Zhejiang University](https://applyforchina.com/id/universities/zhejiang-university/) (Hangzhou)**

**Zhejiang University** is one of the **best AI universities in China**. It is located in Hangzhou, a major technology city and the home of **Alibaba**. This gives students access to a strong digital economy and a fast-growing AI ecosystem.

The university has strong AI-related research in computer science, autonomous systems, neural networks, smart cities, cloud computing, and intelligent platforms. Students interested in **Zhejiang University** artificial intelligence often choose it for its strong academic base and links with Hangzhou’s tech industry.

Zhejiang University is a good choice for students who want:

* industry links with local technology companies
* AI and computer science training
* access to Hangzhou’s tech ecosystem
* smart city and cloud computing research
* autonomous systems and neural networks

### **5. [Nanjing University](https://applyforchina.com/universities/nanjing-university/) (Nanjing)**

**Nanjing University** is one of China’s oldest and most respected universities. It has a strong reputation in both theoretical and applied artificial intelligence.

Its AI-related strengths include machine learning, data mining, natural language processing, cognitive science, and interdisciplinary AI. Students can also explore how AI connects with linguistics, biology, and other research fields.

Nanjing also offers a good study environment. The city has many universities, a long history, and lower living costs than Beijing or Shanghai.

Nanjing University is a good choice for students who want:

* a strong academic base in a calmer city
* machine learning and AI theory
* natural language processing
* cognitive science
* interdisciplinary AI research

### **6. [University of Science and Technology of China](https://applyforchina.com/id/universities/ustc/) (Hefei)**

The **University of Science and Technology of China**, or USTC, is a research-focused university with strong training in science, engineering, and AI.

USTC has close links with the **Chinese Academy of Sciences**, which gives students access to a serious research environment. Its AI-related strengths include AI theory, automation, robotics, quantum technology, and intelligent systems.

This university is a strong option for students who plan to continue to a master’s, PhD, or research institute role.

USTC is a good choice for students who want:

* preparation for graduate research
* deep AI research training
* automation and robotics
* AI theory and intelligent systems
* links with the Chinese Academy of Sciences

### **7. [Beihang University](https://applyforchina.com/ru/universities/beihang-university/?cst) (Beijing)**

**Beihang University** is well known for aerospace, engineering, and advanced technology. Its AI programs are especially useful for students who want to connect artificial intelligence with aviation, drones, robotics, and smart transport.

The university’s AI strengths include robotics, unmanned aerial vehicles, computer vision, intelligent control, and real-time AI systems. Its Beijing location also helps students access research labs, companies, and national technology projects.

Beihang University is a good choice for students who want:

* AI study in Beijing
* aerospace AI
* robotics and drones
* computer vision
* intelligent control systems

### **8. [Harbin Institute of Technology](https://applyforchina.com/universities/harbin-institute-of-technology-2/) (Harbin)**

**Harbin Institute of Technology**, or HIT, is one of China’s leading engineering universities. It has a strong reputation in engineering, space technology, robotics, and applied AI.

Its AI-related areas include intelligent control, pattern recognition, robotics, advanced data analytics, and engineering AI. HIT also has a strong technical culture, so it suits students who prefer labs, research projects, and practical engineering work.

Harbin has colder weather than many Chinese cities. However, living costs can be lower than in Beijing or Shanghai.

HIT is a good choice for students who want:

* a focused technical study environment
* engineering AI
* robotics and automation
* intelligent control
* pattern recognition

### **9. [Xidian University](https://applyforchina.com/universities/xidian-university/) (Xi’an)**

**Xidian University** may be less famous outside China, but it has a strong reputation in electronics, information engineering, communications, and cybersecurity.

Its AI-related strengths include intelligent information processing, neural networks, biometric systems, signal processing, and AI security. This makes Xidian a strong option for students who want to study AI with cyber systems, electronic information, or communications technology.

Xi’an also offers a large student community, rich history, and lower living costs than China’s largest cities.

Xidian University is a good choice for students who want:

* a more affordable study city
* AI and cybersecurity
* intelligent information processing
* signal processing
* biometric systems
* electronics and communications

### **10. [Fudan University](https://applyforchina.com/universities/fudan-university-acceptance-rate-scholarships/) (Shanghai)**

**Fudan University** is one of China’s best-known universities. It has a strong academic reputation and a balanced approach to technology, science, and the humanities.

Its AI-related fields include machine learning, natural language processing, data science, medical AI, AI ethics, and AI with social science. Fudan is also a good choice for students who want to apply AI to healthcare, law, media, business, or public policy.

The Shanghai location gives students access to research events, internship networks, and career opportunities in one of China’s most global cities.

Fudan University is a good choice for students who want:

* AI study in Shanghai
* AI and data science
* medical AI
* natural language processing
* AI ethics
* cross-disciplinary AI study

## How to Choose the Best AI Program in China

The best school depends on your goal.

Choose based on:

* degree level
* program language
* tuition budget
* scholarship chance
* city choice
* research area
* career plan

Here is a simple guide:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Study Goal** | **Strong Options** |
| Overall AI research | Tsinghua, Peking, Zhejiang |
| AI in Shanghai | SJTU, Fudan |
| AI and deep research | USTC, Nanjing University |
| AI and robotics | Beihang, HIT |
| AI and cybersecurity | Xidian University |
| AI and tech industry | Zhejiang, SJTU, Tsinghua |

Students who plan to **study AI in China** should also check the course language. English-taught AI programs are available, but many top programs still use Chinese.

## Admission and Scholarship Snapshot

Most AI programs ask for:

* passport
* diploma
* transcripts
* study plan
* recommendation letters
* language certificate
* CV for graduate programs

Chinese-taught programs often require HSK. English-taught programs may require IELTS, TOEFL, Duolingo, or proof of English-medium study.

Some students may also need the [CSCA exam](https://applyforchina.com/universities/csca-exam-china-study-in-china-entrance-exam/), depending on the program and university.

Scholarships may include:

* Chinese Government Scholarship
* provincial scholarships
* city scholarships
* university scholarships

Always check the latest university notice before applying.

## Career Paths After AI Study in China

AI graduates can work in many fields.

Common roles include:

* AI engineer
* machine learning engineer
* data scientist
* robotics engineer
* computer vision engineer
* NLP engineer
* software developer
* AI product manager
* research assistant

A degree from a strong Chinese university can also support future study in China or overseas.

## Best Sources to Check

For better decisions, compare official pages and rankings.

Useful sources include:

* [Tsinghua University College of AI](https://collegeai.tsinghua.edu.cn/en/)

* [U.S. News Artificial Intelligence Rankings in China](https://www.usnews.com/education/best-global-universities/china/artificial-intelligence)

These sources can help students compare research strength. For program language, tuition, and application rules, use the university’s official admission page.

## Apply to AI Programs in China

Applying to **AI programs in China** can feel confusing. Each school has its own deadline, document list, and scholarship rules.

ApplyForChina helps students compare universities, prepare documents, and plan applications.

Students ready to [study in China](https://applyforchina.com/) can contact ApplyForChina for support with school selection and application steps.

AI is transforming classrooms faster than any technology before it, with global student usage jumping from 66% to 92% in a single year, and the AI in education market is projected to soar from $8.3 billion to $32.27 billion by 2030.

But is this explosive growth actually helping students learn, or quietly eroding critical thinking? While AI tutors are helping students learn twice as fast, 95% of college faculty fear overreliance is dulling independent thought.

We have compiled a detailed statistical report on AI adoption, benefits, risks, and market growth in education by collecting data and numbers from credible and trustworthy third-party sources.

## **Key AI In Education Statistics**

* Global student AI usage jumped from 66% to 92% in 2025.

* 53% of K-12 students use AI for homework help.

* AI tutors helped students learn twice as fast as peers.

* 95% of college faculty fear AI causes student overreliance.

* The AI education market will hit $32.27 billion by 2030.

* K-12 teacher AI adoption doubled from 25% to 53% in one year.

## **AI And Education: General Insights**

Adoption is widespread, but governance is patchy. Global student AI usage rose from 66% in 2024 to 92% in 2025, the steepest yearly leap on record per the HEPI Student Generative AI Survey.

Source: [HEPI](https://www.hepi.ac.uk/reports/student-generative-ai-survey-2025/)

A UNESCO survey of more than 450 institutions found that only 10% of schools and universities have formal AI guidelines.

Source: [UNESCO](https://www.unesco.org/en/articles/unesco-survey-less-10-schools-and-universities-have-formal-guidance-ai)

Globally, 86% of students use AI for studies, with 24% reporting daily use.

Source: [Passive Secrets](https://passivesecrets.com/ai-in-education-statistics/)

## **AI In Schools: Adoption And Usage**

K-12 schools are racing to integrate AI but lag in policy. 30% of K-12 students use AI tools at least once per day, and 53% use AI for help with homework.

Source: [Common Sense Media](https://www.commonsensemedia.org/sites/default/files/research/report/2024-the-dawn-of-the-ai-era_final-release-for-web.pdf)

Only 7% of schools worldwide have AI guidance, and 40% of those policies are informal. Of the institutions with AI policies, just 19% offer AI skills training, leaving roughly 5.89% of all schools globally teaching AI literacy.

Source: [Programs.com](https://programs.com/resources/ai-education-statistics/)

In the United States, all 50 states plus Washington, DC, and US territories have reviewed or proposed AI-related education laws by mid-2025.

Source: [NCSL](https://www.ncsl.org/technology-and-communication/artificial-intelligence-2025-legislation)

## **Teachers Using AI**

A survey run by Forbes revealed that 60% of them had implemented AI in their daily teaching practices.

A total of 39% had not implemented or were unsure. Only 1% chose not to reveal.

Teachers’ response to AI implementation is given below in the table:

| **Teacher Response** | **% Respondents** |
| --- | --- |
| Yes | 60% |
| No | 35% |
| Not Sure | 4% |
| Prefer Not Say | 1% |

Teacher adoption surged in the 2024-25 school year. The share of K-12 teachers using generative AI doubled from 25% to 53% between 2023-24 and 2024-25.

Source: [Rand](https://www.rand.org/pubs/research_reports/RRA4180-1.html)

The Gallup-Walton Family Foundation poll of 2,232 US public school teachers found 60% used AI in 2024-25.

Source: [Gallup](https://news.gallup.com/poll/691967/three-teachers-weekly-saving-six-weeks-year.aspx)

Weekly users save an average of 5.9 hours per week, equal to roughly six weeks of reclaimed time across the school year.

Source: [Walton Family Foundation](https://www.waltonfamilyfoundation.org/the-ai-dividend-new-survey-shows-ai-is-helping-teachers-reclaim-valuable-time)

## **Students Using AI Statistics**

Student usage has reached near-universal levels. 88% of UK university students used generative AI for assessments in 2025, up from 53% in 2024.

Source: HEPI

ChatGPT leads with 66% student adoption, followed by Grammarly and Microsoft Copilot at 25% each.

Source: [Campus Technology](https://campustechnology.com/articles/2024/08/28/survey-86-of-students-already-use-ai-in-their-studies.aspx)

Around 54% of students use AI daily or weekly, while 86% have used it at least once for school tasks ([Codegnan](https://codegnan.com/ai-in-education-statistics/)).

Based on a survey of 3,801 U.S. college students pursuing associate or bachelor’s degrees, the percentage using AI on a daily or weekly basis for each specific purpose was:

| **Educational Purpose** | **% Using Daily or Weekly** |
| --- | --- |
| Getting help with coursework they don’t understand | 64% |
| Checking answers on homework or assignments | 60% |
| Editing or improving writing | 54% |
| Summarizing lectures or notes | 54% |
| Generating new ideas (e.g., paper topics) | 49% |
| Doing research for papers | 45% |
| Creating images and visualizations | 37% |
| Writing papers | 36% |
| Getting career advice | 35% |

Source: Gallup

## **AI In Higher Education**

Higher education has emerged as the highest-adoption segment. 92% of university students used AI tools in 2025, up from 66% in 2024.

Source: HEPI

College usage outpaces school-level adoption, with 82% of college students using AI compared to 58% of high schoolers.

Source: [PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/quizlets-state-of-ai-in-education-survey-reveals-higher-education-is-leading-ai-adoption-302195348.html)

As per UNESCO, 70% of higher-education institutions in Europe and North America have or are developing AI guidance, versus only 45% in Latin America and the Caribbean.

Source: [Engageli](https://www.engageli.com/blog/ai-in-education-statistics)

## **AI In College Usage**

Talking about AI usage in college, more than half of the surveyed students did not have any experience with using AI tools or did not intend to use any for help with assignments or exams (57% each).

Students’ responses to AI usage in college is given below:

| **Survey Statement** | **No** | **Yes** | **Prefer Not To Say** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| I have experience using ChatGPT or similar AI applications. | 57% | 43% | 0% |
| I use or have used AI tools like ChatGPT for my own personal projects, out of curiosity, or just for fun. | 4% | 39% | 0% |
| I use or have used AI tools such as ChatGPT to help complete my assignments or exams. | 20% | 22% | 1% |
| I intend to use, or continue using, AI tools to help complete my assignments or exams. | 57% | 32% | 11% |

Looking at the perceptions of AI results among students, 61% of the respondents say AI tools will become the new normal.

Contrastingly, only 12% disagree with the opinion.

Refer to the table below for perceptions of AI results among students:

| **Statement** | **Disagree** | **Neutral** | **Agree** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AI tools like ChatGPT are virtually undetectable by my instructors. | 33% | 36% | 31% |
| AI tools like ChatGPT generate better results than I can produce on my own. | 35% | 29% | 36% |
| AI tools like ChatGPT generate accurate and reliable results. | 20% | 37% | 43% |
| The importance or impact of AI tools like ChatGPT has been exaggerated in the media. | 21% | 31% | 48% |
| AI tools like ChatGPT generate results that can pass as “human”. | 16% | 33% | 51% |
| In the long term, AI tools like ChatGPT will become the new normal. | 12% | 27% | 61% |

Source: [Best Colleges](https://www.bestcolleges.com/research/college-students-ai-tools-survey/)

## **Benefits Of AI In Education Statistics**

The benefits are measurable. A 2025 Harvard physics study found that students using AI tutors learned more than twice as much in less time than their peers in active-learning classrooms.

Source: [Research Square](https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-4243877/v1)

Students using an enhanced AI tutor showed a 127% improvement versus 48% with a standard chatbot.

Source: [APA](https://www.apa.org/ed/precollege/psychology-teacher-network/introductory-psychology/learning-artificial-intelligence)

Around 90% of educators believe generative AI improves accessibility and personalized learning, and 44% report reduced workload.

Source: [Imagine Learning](https://www.imaginelearning.com/press/report-finds-educators-see-ai-beacon-for-accessible-education/)

Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat usage drove a 15% increase in passing rates and a 12% drop in dropout rates.

Celebrating this mark, Chair of the School, Dr. James Thomas, commented:

“We complete tasks in minutes instead of hours. If just 15% of our more than 6,000 employees save 12 minutes a day, that’s nearly 50,000 hours a year,  time reinvested in meaningful work.”

Source: [Microsoft](https://www.microsoft.com/en/customers/story/23284-miami-dade-college-microsoft-365-copilot#section-block-body)

Macquarie University students using AI chatbots saw exam scores improve by up to 10%.

Source: [Microsoft 2](https://news.microsoft.com/source/asia/2025/03/24/macquarie-university-students-exam-scores-up-by-nearly-10-per-cent-thanks-to-new-ai-powered-chatbot/)

## **Negative Effects Of AI In Education Statistics**

Risks have scaled with the adoption of AI in education. 95% of college faculty fear student overreliance on AI and diminished critical thinking, per the AAC&U national survey.

Source: [AACU](https://www.aacu.org/newsroom/national-survey-95-of-college-faculty-fear-student-overreliance-on-ai-and-diminished-critical-thinking-among-learners-who-use-generative-ai-tools)

According to Gallup, 57% of teachers say AI decreases student independent thinking, and 52% report a decline in critical thinking.

Source: [The 74 Million](https://www.the74million.org/article/survey-60-of-teachers-used-ai-this-year-and-saved-up-to-6-hours-of-work-a-week/)

Nearly 7,000 UK university students were formally caught cheating with AI in 2023-24, triple the previous year, climbing to 7.5 cases per 1,000 students by 2024-25.

Source: [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/education/2025/jun/15/thousands-of-uk-university-students-caught-cheating-using-ai-artificial-intelligence-survey)

An overwhelming 96% of K–12 teachers in the U.S. report receiving no formal training in AI, while 85% say they feel unprepared to manage the use of generative AI in their classrooms effectively.

Source: [ElectroIQ](https://electroiq.com/stats/ai-in-education-statistics/)

Almost two-thirds of surveyed teachers reported plagiarism as the biggest concern in AI in education.

Another concern, cited by just a few teachers, was reduced human interaction while learning. Surprisingly, 4% of the teachers seemed to have no concern with AI.

| **Concern** | **Percentage of Teachers** |
| --- | --- |
| Plagiarism in essays/work | 65% |
| Reduced human interaction in learning | 62% |
| Data privacy and security | 42% |
| Unequal access to AI-powered resources | 30% |
| Job displacement for teachers | 30% |
| Automation of manual tasks | 23% |
| None (no concerns) | 4% |
| Other | 1% |
| Not sure | 1% |

Source: [AIPRM](https://www.aiprm.com/ai-in-education-statistics/)

## **AI In Education Market Size And Growth**

The AI in Education Market stood at $8.3 billion in 2025 and is expected to climb to $32.27 billion, at a 25.9% CAGR.

| **Year** | **Estimated Market Size** |
| --- | --- |

| 2030 | $57.2 billion |

North America held the highest share of revenue at 37.5% in 2025. This translates to approximately $3.1 billion.

Source: [Grand View Research](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/artificial-intelligence-ai-education-market-report)

## **Future Of AI In Education**

Just a little over half of the people surveyed by EdWeek Research Center say that AI in education will increase a little in the future, whereas 43% believe it will remain the same as now.

The table below gives a breakdown of the perceived future of AI in education:

Per Microsoft’s 2025 AI in Education Report, upskilling employees in AI is the top workforce strategy for 47% of leaders over the next 12 to 18 months.

Source: Microsoft

The Josh Bersin Company reports that the $400 billion corporate learning market is being reshaped by AI-driven personalized training that delivers faster completion and better retention.

# AI In Education Statistics (2026): Adoption & Usage Data

## Key Highlights
Global student AI usage jumped from 66% to 92% in 2025, marking the steepest yearly leap on record. The AI in education market is projected to grow from $8.3 billion (2025) to $32.27 billion by 2030 at a 25.9% CAGR, with some projections reaching $136.79 billion by 2035.

## Adoption & Usage
- **K-12 Schools**: 30% of K-12 students use AI tools daily; 53% use AI for homework help. K-12 teacher AI adoption doubled from 25% to 53% between 2023-24 and 2024-25.
- **Teachers**: 60% of US public school teachers used AI in 2024-25. Weekly users save an average of 5.9 hours per week (roughly six weeks of reclaimed time per school year).
- **Higher Education**: 92% of university students used AI tools in 2025 (up from 66% in 2024). 88% of UK university students used generative AI for assessments in 2025. ChatGPT leads with 66% student adoption, followed by Grammarly and Microsoft Copilot at 25% each.
- **College Students**: 64% use AI daily/weekly for coursework help, 60% for checking answers, 54% for editing writing, 54% for summarizing lectures. 61% believe AI tools will become the new normal.

## Benefits
- Harvard physics study (2025): Students using AI tutors learned more than twice as much in less time than peers in active-learning classrooms.
- Enhanced AI tutor showed 127% improvement vs 48% with standard chatbot.
- 90% of educators believe AI improves accessibility and personalized learning; 44% report reduced workload.
- Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat drove 15% increase in passing rates and 12% drop in dropout rates at Miami Dade College.
- Macquarie University students using AI chatbots saw exam scores improve by up to 10%.

## Negative Effects & Risks
- 95% of college faculty fear student overreliance on AI and diminished critical thinking (AAC&U survey).
- 57% of teachers say AI decreases student independent thinking; 52% report decline in critical thinking.
- Nearly 7,000 UK university students formally caught cheating with AI in 2023-24 (triple the previous year).
- 96% of K-12 US teachers received no formal AI training; 85% feel unprepared to manage AI in classrooms.
- Top teacher concerns: Plagiarism (65%), reduced human interaction (62%), data privacy (42%).

## Governance & Policy
- Only 10% of schools and universities have formal AI guidelines (UNESCO survey of 450+ institutions).
- Only 7% of schools worldwide have AI guidance; 40% of those policies are informal.
- Just 19% of institutions with AI policies offer AI skills training.
- All 50 US states plus DC have reviewed or proposed AI-related education laws by mid-2025.

## Market Projections
- North America held 37.5% of global AI education revenue in 2025 (~$3.1 billion).
- Global AI edtech market projected to reach $92.09 billion by 2033.
- 47% of leaders identify AI upskilling as top workforce strategy over next 12-18 months.
